talks.title: Automated Tear Machines: The Reality of ATM Hacking
talks.teaser: Meadow Ellis demystifies ATM security architecture, explaining internal components, cash dispenser controllers, and why legitimate ATM research is so difficult.
talks.summary:
The Anatomy of Modern Automated Teller Machines

Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) combine industrial embedded hardware, specialized cash dispensing mechanisms, and legacy operating systems into high-value street-level physical targets.

Deconstructing ATM Modules and Internal Buses

Meadow Ellis breaks down core ATM subsystems—including cash dispensers, encrypted PIN pads (EPP), card readers, and CEN/XFS software middleware.

Analyzing Physical and Logical Attack Vectors

Ellis reviews common threat models—ranging from physical black-box jackpotting and skimming to software malware injection and transaction hijacking.

The Barriers to Independent ATM Security Research

The author discusses the severe legal, regulatory, and cost hurdles facing researchers attempting to acquire and safely audit ATM hardware.

talks.title: ATM Transaction Reversal Frauds: Cashing Out Without Malware
talks.teaser: Hector Cuevas Cruz explains Transaction Reversal Frauds (TRF), an attack that abuses banking operational rules to cash out ATMs without malware or drilling.
talks.summary:
The Mechanics of Transaction Reversal Fraud (TRF)

Transaction Reversal Fraud (TRF) is a sophisticated physical-logical attack where criminals exploit business logic error-handling rules in ATMs to steal cash with zero net balance deduction.

Abusing Dispenser Error Handling and Sensor Timing

Hector Cuevas Cruz explains how manipulating the shutter during note presentation triggers an intentional timeout, tricking the ATM into reporting an uncollected cash fault.

Automated Account Reversals and Cash Theft

Because the host bank automatically reverses the debit transaction when an uncollected fault is logged, the attacker retains the physical cash while restoring their account balance.

Hardening ATM Shutter Timing and Host Reconciliation

The author provides banking institutions with dispenser sensor telemetry rules, dual-audit logging, and backend reconciliation controls to mitigate TRF attacks.
